standards.mechanism: CREATE DATABASE ... OWNER needs the creator to be able to SET ROLE to the owner
GRANT role TO CURRENT_USER WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT TRUE; a member of the owning role may GRANT and REVOKE on the owner's objects
Membership privileges flow only through INHERIT; SET allows SET ROLE
A non-superuser CREATEROLE creator gets an implicit 'WITH ADMIN TRUE, SET FALSE, INHERIT FALSE' grant (why plain PostgreSQL also fails without the GRANT)
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE only for roles one is a member of
DROP DATABASE only by the database owner (README recovery relies on the kept, inheriting grant)

assumptions: INHERIT TRUE, not the brief's INHERIT FALSE (see conflicts). Evidence: with INHERIT FALSE the init on the non-superuser master printed 'WARNING:  no privileges could be revoked for "disputedesk"' (and for zitadel and public), 'no privileges were granted', then failed with 'ERROR:  permission denied to change default privileges'. PostgreSQL GRANT lets a non-owner grant and revoke on an object only as a member of the owning role, and membership privileges flow only through INHERIT (role-membership).

The master keeps the grant; the script does not REVOKE it. Reasons: a revoke would add no boundary, because a CREATEROLE master can grant itself the role again (it holds the implicit ADMIN grant on plain PostgreSQL, and the RDS probe showed the GRANT succeeds there); and the README's 'A half-done database init' runs DROP DATABASE as dbmaster, which only the owner may do (DROP DATABASE docs), so it needs the inheriting membership. This is the end state story 7.5 chose with createrole_self_grant=set,inherit.

The fixture's plain PostgreSQL 18.6 master holds an implicit ADMIN-only membership in the roles it creates; RDS's holds none. Both lack SET, so both fail the same way without the GRANT. That the GRANT succeeds on RDS rests on the probe in the brief (SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE); INHERIT TRUE is assumed to pass the same check, since a grant's options do not change who may grant.

conflicts: The brief's step 2 specifies 'WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE'. It fails on a non-superuser master: the init's later GRANT, REVOKE and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES act as the owner and need INHERIT (test output above). Keeping INHERIT FALSE would mean running those statements under SET ROLE <owner> and changing the README's recovery, which needs owner privileges for DROP DATABASE. Built with INHERIT TRUE, the simpler correct option; a human may prefer the SET ROLE variant.
